defaults() - Static method in record class io.mavlink4j.config.MavlinkSettings.SigningSettings
A frame counts as "signed recently" for 5s (the link-quality decay window); a signature timestamp up to 1 minute behind the local clock is still accepted (clock skew across a fresh link); the local signing clock persists at most once a minute (mavlink.io's own "ideally at least once a minute" recommendation); at most 256 concurrent (sysid, compid, signingLinkId) streams are tracked for replay detection.

FakeVehicle - Class in io.mavlink4j.testkit
A scripted aircraft over real UDP loopback: it dials the system under test, sends a heartbeat every 200 ms by default (one heartbeat can be lost on plain UDP while the far side is still binding, so the stream never stops), records every frame it receives, and answers on demand or by script.

SerialLink - Class in io.mavlink4j.transport
A serial (jSerialComm-backed) MavlinkLink — modelled line-for-line on TcpClientLink: SerialLink.preservesMessageBoundaries() is honestly false (one SerialLink.poll(java.time.Duration) may return less than one frame, more than one, or a frame split across several polls, exactly like a TCP stream), id is stable for the port's whole life ("serial:" + portDescriptor), and SerialLink.send(byte[], int, int, io.mavlink4j.transport.LinkPeer)'s target parameter is accepted for interface uniformity only — a serial wire has exactly one destination, the far end of the cable, which SerialLink.defaultTarget() honestly reports as LinkPeer.NONE (a serial link has no addressable network peer at all, unlike UDP/TCP).

SigningClock - Class in io.mavlink4j.codec
The MAVLink 2 signing timestamp for one remote system (VERIFIED, mavlink.io message-signing spec): a 48-bit counter in 10 microsecond ticks since SigningClock.SIGNING_EPOCH, not Unix epoch -- a naive millisecond- or microsecond-since-1970 implementation produces a value that looks plausible and fails every verification silently (QA item 3).
SigningClock(InstantSource, LongSupplier, LongConsumer, Duration) - Constructor for class io.mavlink4j.codec.SigningClock
 
SigningClocks - Interface in io.mavlink4j.codec
One SigningClock per remote system id -- a signing timestamp is a per-vehicle fact (two vehicles must never share a monotonic counter), never a process-wide one.
SigningKeyResolver - Interface in io.mavlink4j.codec
The sysid→key lookup the library cannot own: which 32-byte secret belongs to which vehicle is the host application's knowledge (a key store, a device registry), so the host supplies the implementation and the library only consumes the interface.
SigningPolicy - Interface in io.mavlink4j.codec
Decides whether a decoded frame is dispatched, given its origin sysid and SignatureStatus.

TxScheduler - Interface in io.mavlink4j.session
Runs named periodic TX tasks (heartbeat emission, RC override relay, ...) on one shared thread pool rather than one hand-rolled thread loop per feature, so every periodic sender shares one thread lifecycle.

A live TxScheduler.repeat(java.lang.String, java.time.Duration, java.lang.Runnable) registration.
